claims.head: A tough night ahead for Kaprizov
claims.call: The Jets’ P2 (DeMelo and Samberg) spends at least 50% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Jets keep sending DeMelo and Samberg out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Eriksson Ek, Kaprizov and Boldy.

claims.gist: At home, Scott Arniel likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Wild’s first line.

claims.head: The Wild played last night
claims.body: It’s the Wild’s second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Jets get more of the play than usual.

claims.head: In close against from distance
claims.body: The Wild get in close, but the Jets mostly shoot from distance. Minnesota is near the top of the league for shots from in close, and Winnipeg is near the bottom. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Wild to do more of their damage around the net.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 6 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 47%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
M. Foligno is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
B. Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman.
J. Morrissey is day to day (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. D. Samberg has taken his spot beside D. DeMelo.

WPG.head: Nothing to separate these two
WPG.body: Minnesota is on the second night of a back-to-back, while Winnipeg has home-ice advantage. Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Winnipeg may be without Morrissey, though. Winnipeg can tip it if their power play gets going.

MIN.head: Too close to call
MIN.body: Minnesota is on the second night of a back-to-back, while Winnipeg has home-ice advantage. Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Winnipeg may be without Morrissey, though. Minnesota can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.
